title: Unethical Price Hike After Years of Loyalty. Overnight, Sortly More Than Doubled My Subscription $
text:
I’ve been a Sortly customer for 5–6 years, paying $1,180 a year for their Ultra plan. Last year, without my permission, they increased my payment and moved me to a higher rate. After multiple emails, they admitted the mistake, apologized, and moved me back.

Now, I’ve received a 30-day notice that my plan will jump to about $2,800 a year — more than double overnight — with no real choice other than cutting off many of my items to qualify for a cheaper tier, or paying the inflated price. When I went to cancel by subscription, I was suddenly offered 40% off. This just confirms their strategy: wait until customers have built up large inventories (I have about 3,600 items) and then force them into paying drastically higher rates, knowing it will be a big inconvenience to switch.

Thankfully, I already have all my data zipped, exported to PDF, and my IT team is moving me to a new system. I’d rather spend time and money transitioning than give Sortly another penny.

This company is greedy and unethical. They care more about squeezing customers than offering fair value. I barely used most of their features, just inventory tracking and adding a few items a month lately. I don’t recommend Sortly to anyone — and I wouldn’t be surprised if more negative reviews keep rolling in.

Sortly lured me in like many others with friendly pricing, slick marketing, and promises of “unlimited” Pro version. I invested years setting up my entire inventory system on their platform.

Worse still, I later found out I wasn’t alone. Hundreds of users across forums are reporting the same experience. Small businesses, home users - all targeted, all squeezed. This isn’t a misunderstanding. It’s a deliberate ramp-and-dump scheme.

They bet you’ll be too invested to leave. That you’ll just accept the extortion to avoid losing your data. This is digital hostage taking, and it’s happening in plain sight.

Sortly’s business model is a warning sign. If you’re thinking about trying them - don’t. If you’re already in - get out while you still can. And to Sortly: You know exactly what you’re doing. If you want this review taken down, make it right not just for me, but for every customer you ambushed.

text:
CAUTION!! We are a home staging business and our first year subscription was $1,068 for the Ultra plan we were told 11 days prior to the annual renewal the subscription would now be $2,700/yr. 

The Ultra Plan currently is being advertised as including 10,000 entires, 25 custom fields, and 5 user licenses for $708/yr.

When I requested more information about the rate increase via email we were told “We are in the process of reconfiguring our plans.” Sortly will not be adding any additional features or options to justify the increase.

And while I could go on about the app and the lack of features and ease of use - save yourself the trouble and sign up with Stageforce. They have been in business for over 20 years and have an excellent track record. I have never heard of a company that would days before their annual renewal increase their subscriptions by over 250%. We initially chose Sortly because we prioritized the ability to scan with our phones vs needing RFID tags and scanners. Huge mistake! The items need to be searched by manually typing the item name. The scanning is limited to one folder at a time and multiple steps are needed to change the folder to scan.

It’s really disappointing that we invested so much time integrating our business to use their system. For a year we overlooked their shortcomings but charging 2.5x more for an inadequate system is too far. Hopefully, you take our advice and this doesn’t happen to you too.

title: Good app, but costs more than your phone!
text:
I’ve been playing around with a lot of inventory apps to keep track of home electronics and other items, mainly to have insurance logs and records of serial numbers, etc.

I was impressed by the simplicity of Sortlys interface, but quickly ran into the frustrating limits of the free version: no more than 100 items, and only 1 custom field. Note that there are almost no fields available to use by default, you need to customize the items by adding the custom fields. So by adding a serial number as my only field I couldn’t track any other attribute of my items.

That’s where I find Sorty falls short for me: you have to pay for the premium version to really make use of the app, and the free version didn’t allow me to really test it out (maybe keep the item limit but get rid of the field limit?)

Now, I would happily pay for an app like this! I have plenty of subscriptions to useful home utility apps like shared password managers, etc. But the cheapest subscription is $50/mo!!! There is nothing that this app could possibly do that makes it more valuable than the cell phone on which it is running, or the network plan your phone is using! This app is obviously targeting business users, that much is clear when you use it as most of the content describes inventory and business uses, and I’m sure this cost is reasonable in that environment.

Sortly really needs to rethink their Freemium model and how they structure their pricing. There are plenty of SaaS apps like this that have successfully bridged personal and enterprise use by structuring their subscriptions the right way. They seem to be succeeding for the time being by price gauging the market with customers who can afford to pay the cost, but their $50/mo subscription feels more like a $5/mo subscription compared to the value of other similar services.

text:

I first downloaded this app a couple of months ago to give it a try after reading that it was a great home inventory solution.  Unfortunately, starting a home inventory is one of those tasks that is easy to put off and I ran out of time on the free trial before I had a chance to try it out.  I wasn’t ready to pay an annual subscription (around $50 under their old plan) without kicking the tires first, but when I contacted support and asked for an extension of my 2 week trial period, they were unable to help me.  I figured I’d continue with the “free” version and then subscribe if I liked it. 

Fast forward two months, and I carved out some time to really dig in.  Lo and behold, their subscription model has completely changed!  There is still a free tier, which is admittedly much more functional than before—you can now use the web interface to easily edit and tag your items, which is great.  Unfortunately, there is now a limit of 110 items unless you subscribe to the pro version (2000 items) for $40 *a month*.  110 items is simply not enough to catalog even my 2-bedroom apartment; towards the end, I was combining like items and approximating their total value, then adding additional details in the notes.  

Though I thought ~$50 a year (their old plan) was a lot considering its purpose, I’d gladly pay a reasonable annual subscription fee for this app.  Instead of 110 item and 2000 item tiers, how about something in between—perhaps 250 items for $25 a year?  Market the pro version to true pros, keep the free version, and then have a middle tier.

text:
I started using this app after my other one was no longer compatible with newer phone updates. It does the job that I need (small business inventory) but in order to be the best there needs to be a few updates. 
1. The camera view doesn't match the picture that is snapped. I have to get really close to objects to not show the background because the snapped picture captures more than what is seen on the phone display (I do not have this problem on my regular phone camera.) This only became a problem with the last couple of app updates. 
2. I wish we could edit/add entry spaces "attributes" on the objects. Example: for one folder every object has a size. I wish we could add a spot that is always there that I could just tap or select from a dropdown menu with the options pertaining to that attribute (S,M,L etc). 
3. The tags are unhelpful. They should be used to help search so the name of the objects aren't extremely long, which mine are. I don't like how all the tags from every listing are there in a list because it wastes time looking for the one I need and is just not user friendly. Sometimes only one or two objects share the same tag but it adds a spot to the list making it extremely long. Having attributes would help with this too. 4. I don't like how tapping on an item to view better automatically puts it in edit mode. This subtracts a star by itself. Tapping an object should put it in view mode and there should be an edit button to edit. 
Overall, this app does what I need but my previous one was better. I really hope these suggestions are really taken into consideration. I know this app is for general inventory but these suggestions could open up the customer base to specific inventory needs.
